key_insight: GenEHR learns from longitudinal EHR timelines, including irregular visit spacing, to predict who is at elevated risk of a first cancer diagnosis within five years.
clinical_relevance: The model may help prioritize patients for risk-based cancer screening and earlier evaluation, especially for aggressive cancers such as pancreatic and ovarian cancer.
method: Autoregressive generative model trained on millions of EHR patient histories
Explicitly models irregular time intervals between visits
Uses parameter-efficient supervised adaptation for pan-cancer risk stratification
evidence_signal: In five large EHR cohorts, supervised adaptation substantially improved prediction of first cancer diagnosis within a five-year horizon.
watch_item: The findings are retrospective, so prospective validation is still needed before clinical decision-support use.
paper_title: Identifying cohorts at elevated risk of cancers using generative modeling of patient health states
